My reasoning:

I am old, 70 years now, and my wife and I manage just these 2 mu. My son is in town, he does not farm. So I keep things simple, same as last year and the year before. Fifty years I have done this, wheat after maize, maize after wheat, no change.

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I buy the improved seed from the county store — everyone here plants Jimai, the dealer picks a good one. Before planting I put one bag of compound fertilizer, 15-15-15, plus some diammonium, on the 2 mu. Then when wheat greens up in March I topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu. My neighbors put a little more, but I think this is enough — I don't want to waste money, but I also don't want thin wheat. Better a little extra than a poor harvest. I plough the field after maize to bury the stubble, then sow.

Water from my well — I irrigate at sowing to press the soil, once in winter if dry, then green-up, jointing, and filling. Four or five times. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and for aphids in April. Two sprays is enough usually.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. No tilling, just push the seed into the stubble — saves diesel, saves time. Zhengdan hybrid seed, what the dealer sells. One bag of compound at planting, then urea at the big trumpet stage. Summer rain does most of the watering, I only irrigate once or twice if July is dry. Spray once for borers.

Wheat I get about 450 kg per mu, maize about 550. Same as always.
